I will keep my full 6.0 mu in the usual wheat-maize rotation, because that is the system I know best and it fits my land, labor, and well irrigation. I have farmed for 30 years, my household is small, and some labor is off-farm, so I will choose steady, familiar management instead of anything complicated. For winter wheat, I will use improved seed, apply a moderate amount of fertilizer, irrigate a few key times, and keep pesticide use limited but timely, because wheat here needs stable water and nutrition to hold yield. After wheat harvest, I will plant summer maize on the same 6.0 mu, use hybrid seed for stronger yield, give it more nitrogen than wheat, irrigate when rainfall is not enough, and control pests with a small number of sprays. I will use rotary tillage because it is practical for my scale, saves time, and fits the rotation.
